name: Margaret Thatcher
role: UK Prime Minister (1979-1990) and Conservative Party leader (1975-1990)
summary: Thatcher advocated free markets, privatisation, lower taxes, curbs on trade union power and a smaller state role in industry, while keeping the NHS and a strong police and defence. She held socially conservative views on family, crime and immigration, backed NATO and nuclear deterrence, and opposed deeper European integration and sanctions on apartheid South Africa. She voted for some 1960s liberalising bills and supported the death penalty for terrorism.

universal-healthcare.rationale: 1979 manifesto stated no intention to cut NHS spending and sought to improve the tax-funded service while allowing private care alongside it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Called free enterprise and competition the engines of prosperity and said central planning and detailed control do not work.

public-ownership.rationale: Led a privatisation programme, saying eighteen state enterprises had been handed back by 1988 and that more nationalisation would impoverish the country.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Pledged to cut the top income tax rate to the European average and rejected Labour's proposed wealth tax.

unions-good.rationale: Said a strong, responsible union movement could help recovery, while arguing unions had been given excessive privileges and legislating to curb them.

property-fundamental.rationale: Inferred: she called wider ownership of homes and shares one of her proudest achievements; she did not describe property as very hard to override.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: she promised to reduce government intervention and over-government in industry, though she said privatised monopolies must not exploit consumers.

cut-welfare.rationale: Said benefits meant as a safety net had encouraged people to look to society rather than themselves; her government also raised social security spending.

state-harmful.rationale: Sought a smaller state but assigned it core roles such as defence, law and welfare; she did not call it unnecessary.

limit-guns.rationale: Announced tougher action against knives and guns in 1987.

empower-police-military.rationale: Promised to spend more on crime and police pay and increase defence spending.

decide-locally.rationale: Abolished the GLC and metropolitan councils and sought to cut local authority power over tenants, schools and business.

rehabilitation.rationale: Called for really tough sentences for violent offenders and a short, sharp shock regime, with some alternative sentences.

traditional-family.rationale: Said the family is where habits of mutual love, tolerance and service are learned and on which every healthy nation depends.

abortion-legal.rationale: Voted for the 1967 Steel bill legalising abortion.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Said people feared Britain being swamped by a different culture, and valued her national character and identity.

gradual-change.rationale: Described her government as one of the truly radical ministries, while valuing institutions such as Parliament and the Lords.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Promised firm immigration control, a quota system and tighter entry rules, and spoke of fear of being swamped.

free-trade.rationale: Argued Europe must not be protectionist and rejected import controls.

nation-first.rationale: Stressed sovereignty and national interest but also urged common international action on shared problems.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: In 1992 she called for NATO action to stop the Serbian assault in Bosnia and end ethnic cleansing.

open-borders.rationale: Rejected anything but tightly controlled entry and promised a quota on settlement.

limit-growth.rationale: Said the choice is not industrial development or a clean environment: we need both.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called for a climate convention in 1988-89, but later reportedly revised her view; the mixed record gives no clear current stance.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Called nuclear power the most environmentally safe energy and backed a larger programme.

central-planning.rationale: Stated that central planning and detailed control do not work and that a state-controlled economy means low growth.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Promised to deal with the most damaging features of capital transfer and capital gains taxes and move to a lighter capital tax system.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Rejected import controls as raising prices and inviting retaliation, and said Europe should not be protectionist.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Wrote that government strategies, plans and subsidies cannot produce revival and promised to cut National Enterprise Board powers.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Made a property-owning democracy a central aim, through council-house sales, share ownership and employee share schemes.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Rejected Labour's social contract and incomes policies, saying private-sector pay bargaining should be left to the firms and workers concerned.

one-party-rule.rationale: Said communism was in retreat and that democracy and free enterprise alone meet people's needs; she criticised one-party Soviet rule.

democracy-best.rationale: Held democracy and free enterprise to be what meets people's needs; her remarks do not address voters choosing badly.

direct-votes.rationale: 1979 manifesto promised discussion of referendums, and later she urged a referendum on Maastricht, but she stressed parliamentary supremacy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Said Northern Ireland would stay in the Union unless its majority consented; she did not support a general right of secession.

military-superiority.rationale: Warned of Soviet military superiority and promised significant defence increases.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Blamed Labour for setting one group against another and urged all to be on the same side.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Criticised the politics of envy and aimed to let each child progress as far as ability allows, not to equalise outcomes.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Said there is no entitlement unless someone has first met an obligation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Foreword said the manifesto rested on reason and common sense, not dogma.

direct-action.rationale: Described the miners' strike as an attack on democracy and the rule of law.

production-for-use.rationale: Treated profits as essential to investment and rejected state-planned production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Wrote that profits are the foundation of a free enterprise economy and rejected the politics of envy.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Manifesto said it would be wrong to impose by law a system of worker participation in every company.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Called a gradual reduction of the government borrowing requirement vital and warned that high borrowing raises interest rates and unemployment.

economic-freedom.rationale: Described free enterprise and competition as the guardians of liberty as well as engines of prosperity.

work-for-welfare.rationale: 1979 manifesto said rules requiring the unemployed to accept available jobs would be reinforced and benefit fraud tackled.

class-collaboration.rationale: Wrote that employers, employees, government and public all share an interest in productivity and growth, and criticised setting groups against each other.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Favoured a National Heritage Fund to preserve historic buildings and artistic treasures.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: 1979 manifesto backed a competitive coal industry and encouraged North Sea oil output, though she later stressed greenhouse gas risks.

proportional-representation.rationale: Criticised coalition government as slow and based on trade-offs, valuing a clear majority.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Kept state roles in the NHS, welfare and a national curriculum, saying government must set education standards.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Manifesto said rights of all legally settled British citizens are equal before the law whatever race, colour or creed.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Called competition an engine of prosperity; she did not address struggle between peoples.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Promised and delivered a legal right for council tenants to buy, with discounts rising to 60 per cent; called it a proud achievement.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Her governments restricted secondary picketing, encouraged secret ballots and removed strike immunity without ballots.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Said people might become hostile if they feared being swamped, and tied good community relations to firm immigration control.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Said Labour's price controls achieved only job losses and less consumer choice, and removed controls on prices and pay.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred: she championed free institutions and faulted Soviet-style controls on liberty.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Said cooperation between independent sovereign states is best and rejected a European super-state.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Committed to keeping faith with NATO and allies and to strengthening defence alongside them.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Manifesto set out to revive the private rented sector rather than ban renting.

death-penalty.rationale: Stated an intention to vote for the death penalty for terrorist murder and voted for restoration in the 1980s.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Passed the British Nationality Act to define citizenship more tightly and control entry.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Promised aid but stressed trade and private investment.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Called the independent deterrent vital to security.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Backed the Montreal ozone agreement while saying the full implications of the ozone hole remained unknown.

collective-defense.rationale: Pledged to work with NATO allies; said NATO's purpose is to prevent all war.

common-currency.rationale: Opposed ERM membership and argued against moves to monetary union; her Bruges address focused on practical steps, not a central bank.

no-bailouts.rationale: Manifesto said help for firms in difficulty must be temporary and tapered, with success or failure in their own hands; her record included some rescues.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: she opposed new European regulations that raise employment costs.

moral-incentives.rationale: Argued people needed more material incentive, so that hard work pays and success is rewarded.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Promised to foster Commonwealth links and use its collective influence.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Pledged to restore the supremacy of Parliament as the centre of the nation's decisions.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Said animal welfare concerns us all and promised to update farm animal codes and experiment law.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Backed codes of welfare for farm animals and tighter rules on live animal export and experiments.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Praised the philanthropy of successful people and called for that sense of obligation to the wider community to be enlisted today.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Voted against relaxing divorce law in 1968.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Her government authorised SAS training of non-communist Cambodian resistance forces against Vietnamese-backed rule.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred: she held that lasting jobs come from private-sector growth rather than government preserving or creating employment.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Called the rule of law the basis of a free life and attacked groups that flouted it.

non-intervention.rationale: Used force in the Falklands and urged action in Bosnia, and called for armed action against aggression.

defeat-communism.rationale: Warned against illusory detente in 1976 yet later said she could do business with Gorbachev.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Backed private health insurance and pay-beds alongside the NHS and created independent state-funded schools outside local authority control.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Said free enterprise and competition brought unimagined wealth and shaped free institutions.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Was one of few Conservative MPs to support the Abse bill decriminalising male homosexuality.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Increased defence spending and condemned unilateral disarmament.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anchored British policy in NATO and the Atlantic alliance.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Urged voluntary and self-help groups to work with statutory services and praised philanthropy as a model of community obligation.

rent-control.rationale: Said legislation had driven landlords out of the rented sector and introduced shorthold tenure to free short lettings from restrictive rules.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Deployed US cruise missiles at Greenham Common over mass protests.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Hosted US cruise missiles on British soil.

second-chamber.rationale: Opposed abolishing the Lords, calling a strong second chamber a vital safeguard for democracy.

future-generations.rationale: Said the last thing we want is to leave environmental debts for our children.

arms-reduction.rationale: Backed the INF treaty and 50 per cent cuts in strategic weapons, but said European nuclear cuts had gone far enough.

farm-price-support.rationale: Wanted radical changes to the Common Agricultural Policy, including freezing prices of surplus products.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Pressed ahead with Trident and modernising the independent deterrent while Soviet forces held superiority.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Pushed tougher sentences and appeals against lenient ones, but did not call for fixed sentences.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Her 1979 manifesto and the 1980 and 1982 Employment Acts curtailed the closed shop, requiring overwhelming majority ballots and compensation for those dismissed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Held public office as an MP for 33 years and PM, with no recorded objection to women voting or holding office.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Planned to shift from taxes on earnings to taxes on spending and her first budget raised VAT; she exempted necessities from extension.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Manifesto aimed at concentrating welfare on the old, sick, disabled and those in real need.

notes: Changes of view: she backed an active climate response in 1988-89 and later revised her view (Statecraft, 2002; not read directly, so the answer is 0 at low confidence). Her 1988 Bruges speech hardened her stance on Europe. She opposed sanctions on South Africa (Vancouver press conference), but no statement asks about sanctions. The Margaret Thatcher Foundation site was unreachable directly (Cloudflare 403), so Wayback Machine copies were read. Her Downing Street Years, Path to Power and Statecraft texts were not available.
